Most survivors are literal physics or magic where the noun is the real agent (hum, light, smell, voice carrying), with no hidden human actor: topographic idiom, collective patrol actions with riders on page, and involuntary body responses where involuntariness is the point (L145/L205 fist closing 'without meaning to', L233 palm going cold). secondSweep.scope: Re-read all 295 lines for inanimate or abstract subjects carrying agency, desire, cognition, combustion, or physical-behaviour verbs; roads and geography with motion verbs; receiver nouns with demoted actors; body-part subjects with volition; abstract states settling into body parts; and repeated-subject metaphor chains.
secondSweep.result: One additional kill surfaced (L7 'a fight turned on them'). Roads and tracks (L55, L117, L175) use only topographic extent verbs (bent, dropping, went on, climbing) and none carries orders, promises, or questions. No receiver noun takes a revision or cognition verb while its actor sits in an instrument phrase. The map (L283 'went south with her') names its carrier. Body-part subjects are all involuntary or sensory (L13, L63, L75, L145, L205, L233, L265). No abstract state is settled into a body part. The L275 plan anchor 'palm remembers' is already written as 'In her palm she remembered', with the character as the subject.

findings.text: They always went for water when a fight turned on them, as if running water had ever stopped an arrow.
findings.patternName: Abstraction given an agency verb (fight 'turned on' the trolls)
findings.subject: a fight
findings.realAgent: The Farstrider archers who are winning: the trolls are losing to Sylvanas's patrol.
findings.reason: Pattern 5. The abstraction 'fight' gets the verb of betrayal or attack while the real actors, the rangers killing them, are dropped. Calling it a common idiom is the guide's own named rationalization ('personification is normal'). The plain statement of the trolls' state does the same work and keeps the sardonic second half.
findings.suggestedFix: They always went for water when they were losing, as if running water had ever stopped an arrow.
findings.crossCheckNotes: The trolls ('they') are now the subject. The kept 'as if ... had ever stopped' clause is literal physics in a negated hypothetical, not a pivot. No tic words introduced; simile_as_if count is unchanged at 1 of 5.
